title: Historical Poster Styles

card.teaser: Nine weeks, nine posters: Dada, the Stenberg brothers, Modernism and more.

summary: A nine-poster series exploring historical design movements through distinct approaches to typography, color, collage, grids, and composition.

hero.alt: A grid of posters in historical design styles.

text: This series examines how historical graphic design movements use visual structure to communicate ideas. Each poster responds to a different style or reference, using its typographic and compositional principles to shape a contemporary interpretation.
The goal was not simply to imitate historical aesthetics, but to understand how the choices behind each style affect the way a message is communicated.

rows.heading: Reading the originals
rows.body: For each poster I started with the real thing: a Dada photomontage, a Stenberg brothers poster built on concentric circles, and mid-century book covers made from blocks of flat color and cut paper shapes. I looked at how each one uses type, color and structure to make its point, then chose what to borrow.

rows.heading: Thumbnails first
rows.body: Before any final art, I filled sheets with small black-and-white thumbnails to test where type and image would sit. Some are already close to the finished posters, like Harvest, and a later sheet starts bringing in red.

steps.title: Concept

finalDesign: I wasn't trying to recreate the originals. A copy of a Stenberg poster is just a Stenberg poster. For each one I took the structure, like the grid, the spiral or the cut-up type, and applied it to a subject from now, like *Midsommar* or *Mexican Gothic*. The nine posters share almost nothing on purpose, so each movement's actual moves stay visible.
pull: A copy of a Stenberg poster is just a Stenberg poster.
